output.summary: KEP-3866 proposes a new, officially supported nftables-based backend for kube-proxy on Linux, alongside the existing iptables and ipvs backends. Its status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: iptables has stopped receiving new features and performance work, while nftables has become the successor in the Linux kernel. The KEP proposes a supported nftables backend and explicitly defers replacing iptables or ipvs as the default to a separate future KEP. Its goals also include documenting incompatible behavior and ensuring users can switch modes without manual rule cleanup.

alternatives.option: Keep the iptables backend as the only default and do nothing
alternatives.why_not: The Drawbacks section says doing nothing would leave many users unable to use the default proxy implementation eventually.

alternatives.option: Replace iptables and ipvs with nftables in this KEP and make nftables the default
alternatives.why_not: The summary says replacing or deprecating the existing backends would be handled in a separate future KEP, and the Non-Goals exclude making nftables the default.

alternatives.option: Keep the ipvs backend and avoid adding a new backend
alternatives.why_not: The readme does not compare this option directly; it only notes ipvs as an existing backend and does not explain why it was rejected.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes the creation of a new official/supported nftables backend for kube-proxy.
that replacement/deprecation would be handled in a separate future KEP
Development on iptables has mostly stopped, with new features and performance improvements primarily going into nftables instead.
However, doing nothing would result in a situation where, eventually, many users would be unable to use the default proxy implementation.
